record.paper_title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
record.original_question: Can cross-layer security approaches that protect information across multiple protocol-stack layers improve the security and privacy of air-water communication systems, where such approaches have not yet been studied according to the survey?

evidence.quote: We believe that such approaches have not been studied in air-water communication systems and can potentially improve the security in these systems.

artifact.category_tag: Cross-layer security in air-water wireless communication
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a hybrid air-water wireless communication system that transmits information across the air-water interface using a combination of physical media (e.g., radio-frequency links above water, and acoustic, optical, or magneto-inductive links underwater). The communication protocol is organized as a layered stack (physical, data-link/MAC, network, transport, and application layers), and each layer admits its own security mechanisms (e.g., physical-layer secrecy coding and key generation, link-layer authentication, network-layer routing security, transport-layer encryption, and application-layer access control). A cross-layer security scheme is defined as a protocol that jointly designs and coordinates security mechanisms across two or more of these layers, allowing parameters and information at one layer to inform the security operations at another.

Develop a formal model of an air-water communication system that captures (i) the heterogeneous channel characteristics across the air-water boundary (including refraction, scattering, multipath, and noise statistics of acoustic, optical, and RF sub-channels), (ii) an explicit adversary model with capabilities at each layer (eavesdropping, jamming, spoofing, traffic analysis, and node compromise), and (iii) suitable security and privacy metrics (e.g., secrecy capacity, equivocation, key-generation rate, detection probability of active attacks, and privacy leakage).

Within this model, design cross-layer security protocols that jointly leverage at least two protocol-stack layers, and rigorously establish whether such cross-layer designs can achieve strictly better security and privacy guarantees—under the stated metrics—than any protocol that confines its security mechanisms to a single layer. In particular, determine quantitative conditions on the channel and adversary parameters under which cross-layer schemes outperform single-layer schemes, and identify cases (if any) in which no such improvement is possible.
artifact.status_search_result: A brief search did not surface a definitive study establishing cross-layer security protocols specifically designed and analyzed for air-water (cross-medium) wireless communication systems. Cross-layer security has been studied for underwater acoustic networks and for terrestrial wireless networks, but a comprehensive treatment for hybrid air-water systems appears to remain an open research direction.

status_evidence.title: Underwater and Air-Water Wireless Communication: State-of-the-art, Channel Characteristics, Security, and Open Problems
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys underwater and air-water wireless communication and lists open problems including security and privacy directions.
status_evidence.claim: Cross-layer security for air-water systems is identified as an unaddressed direction.
